ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a single-loop series circuit, with voltage source U on the left; the upper component is labeled Z1, with its impedance marked as 2 Ω beside it; the right component is labeled Z2, marked beside it as (2+j) Ω. The two impedances Z1 and Z2 are connected in series in the same loop. Then reason: The total series impedance is Z_total = Z1 + Z2 = 2 + (2+j) = 4+j Ω, so the real part of the total impedance Re(Z_total)=4 Ω. The problem gives that the active power of the power supply is P=2 W. In a series circuit the current is the same, and the active power of the power supply equals |I|^2 Re(Z_total), therefore |I|^2 = 2/4 = 0.5. The active power of Z1 is P1 = |I|^2 Re(Z1) = 0.5 × 2 = 1 W.
